Rei bene cōtra hostes geredę neglecta occasione. lib.11. epist.12. lib.12. epist.8.9. Sunt huius generis etiam in Epistolis ad Atticum exempla aliqua egregia, maxime lib.11. quas tempore exilii sui Cicero scripsit, & in quibus statum suum miserabilem deplorat: eiusdem quoque culpam, partim in aduersariorum improbitatem, partim credulitatem suam nimiam transfert. Deinde lib.3. epist.4. vbi Cicero de proscriptione sua conqueritur: & 6. eiusdem, in qua aegre hoc admodum molesteq; fert, quod summis suis in doloribus ac miseriis Tarenti Atticum non viderit: nec eius vti consilio potuerit: & 26. in qua lamentari sese merito scribit, propterea quod periisse sese funditus intelligat: & lib.7. epist.8. vbi de Pompeii in gerendo bello negligentia, querela instituitur: & 15. eiusdem, in qua apud

page.notes: Catchword "apud" is at the lower right, below the last line. The text is one continuous paragraph of references, with no indents on this page. The first line continues from the previous page. Printed hyphens kept: "Tyran-nide", "Reno-uato", "tem-pore", "aduersa-riorum", "credulita-tem", "fum-mis" (joined). "pertur-bato" has no visible hyphen at the line end, so it is written whole. "cotra" is read as "cōtra" from its tilde. "geredę" is doubtful (the ę is printed; the word may be "gerēdę"). "exilij" and "Pompeij" are written with final ii per the rule for vowel i. The right edge of the scan is cut off, so the last words of the lines there may be incomplete.
